bullets.title: AVGO beats Q2 but AI revenue guidance disappoints; stock falls ~12% AH
bullets.body: Broadcom reported Q2 FY26 revenue of $22.19B (+48% YoY), adj. EPS $2.44 vs. $2.39 estimate, with AI segment up 143%. However, the market expected a raise to the $100B+ 2027 AI revenue target, which was merely reiterated; Q2 AI semiconductor bookings of $30B vs. $10.8B shipped signal demand is real, but FY26 AI revenue guide of $56B disappointed elevated expectations. One analyst notes demand is 'insatiable' and Broadcom is backing a $36B Apollo/Blackstone SPV for Anthropic chip purchases, framing the miss as a function of multi-sourcing hyperscalers, not demand weakness.

bullets.title: TSMC CEO: supply will fall short of AI demand for years; 30%+ revenue growth reaffirmed
bullets.body: TSMC CEO C.C. Wei at Computex confirmed full-year revenue growth >30%, said global chip supply will fall short of AI demand 'for years,' and sees AI shifting from generative Q&A models toward agentic/command-execution workloads driving more token usage. He confirmed CoPoS advanced packaging on pilot line with meaningful volume ramp in 2-3 years and purchase of High-NA EUV equipment (research only for now). He also said Korean competitors cannot replicate TSMC's model near-term and Taiwan's competitive position will be 'difficult to challenge.'

bullets.title: Goldman raises hyperscaler capex forecast to $5.3T (2025-2030); bullish read-through for upstream semis
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs revised combined capex for Google/Meta/Microsoft/Amazon to $5.3 trillion for 2025-2030, up from a prior $4.5T estimate made at Q1 earnings. One fintwit account noted this is bullish for 'all upstream semi supply chain companies.'

bullets.title: GOOGL equity offering closes multiple times oversubscribed; Berkshire participation seen as AI confidence signal
bullets.body: Alphabet's $85B equity offering closed multiple times oversubscribed. Berkshire Hathaway's participation was described as a 'strong vote of confidence' in Alphabet's AI strategy and signals a shift in AI funding from private to cash-rich public tech companies. Alphabet CFO cited 'unprecedented demand from enterprises and consumers.'

bullets.title: MRVL wins Google TPUv8e custom networking chip deal on Intel 18A; Jensen Huang praises trillion-dollar potential
bullets.body: Marvell received a custom networking chip order from Google for the TPUv8e, to be manufactured on Intel's 18A/18AP process. Separately, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang publicly praised Marvell's trillion-dollar networking/connectivity potential. One analyst notes Qualcomm acquired Alphawave similarly for photonics, paralleling Marvell's Celestial acquisition.

bullets.title: Nvidia Vera Rubin compute trays in mass production at 1/minute at Foxconn; Mizuho raises PT to $300
bullets.body: Foxconn is mass-producing Nvidia Vera Rubin compute trays on fully automated lines at 1 tray per minute—Jensen Huang's first Computex stop signaled the strategic partnership depth. Mizuho raised NVDA price target to $300. NVDA CEO also said 'nobody uses AI better than Meta,' and visited MediaTek, ASUS, ZOTAC, and SKHynix booths. SK Hynix and NVDA CEOs met at GTC Taipei.

bullets.title: HOOD sees $35M+ insider buying in one week as Clarity Act fintech regulation risk looms
bullets.body: HOOD Director Meyer Malka purchased $35.1M of Robinhood shares over the past week (including $15.1M indirectly via Bullfrog Capital), a strong insider confidence signal. Separately, a fintech regulatory threat was flagged: bank-lobbied Clarity Act bills could ban fintech/crypto platform innovation or competition against traditional banks, pressuring HOOD and peers.

bullets.title: NOW shows bullish reversal setup; trader trimmed 20% but plans re-entry on dips
bullets.body: ServiceNow is flagged as forming a higher-high for the first time, signaling a potential trend shift from downtrend to uptrend, with strong confirming volume in a retest phase. A fintwit trader confirms holding NOW, trimmed 20% three days ago to lock gains, and plans to buy again at lower levels.

bullets.title: S&P 500 ends 9-day win streak; Fed's Logan signals potential rate hikes later in 2025
bullets.body: The S&P 500 broke a 9-day win streak, closing down 0.68% to 7,557.87. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said she is 'increasingly concerned' inflation won't return to 2% quickly and indicated rate hikes may be warranted later this year. Markets have now repriced from pricing ~50 bps of cuts by Dec 2026 in Feb to pricing ~20 bps of hikes.

bullets.title: Tech sector P/E expands to 48x from 32x since March low; 3x Semiconductor ETF up 1,550% YoY
bullets.body: S&P Tech sector trailing 12-month P/E jumped from ~32 to 48 since the March 30 low. The 3x Semiconductor ETF is up 1,550% (16x) over the past year—the highest count of Nasdaq 100 stocks with 400%+ 12-month returns since the dot-com bubble (six stocks). Semiconductor stocks have more than doubled YTD. Multiple accounts flagging overbought conditions and market dispersion/correlation extremes.

bullets.title: CSCO pivoting to AI infrastructure platform from legacy networking hardware
bullets.body: Multiple research notes flag Cisco's strategic pivot away from legacy networking toward an AI infrastructure platform/software model. CSCO also hit a new 52-week high during the session, alongside AAPL, MU, AMD, MRVL, SNDK, and VST.

bullets.title: SNDK: Trump's disclosed Jan 5 purchase up 400%+; memory sector rotation noted
bullets.body: President Trump's disclosed January 5th purchase of SanDisk (SNDK) is up over 400% since filing. SNDK also hit a 52-week high intraday. Separately, one analyst notes Hynix ADR/local divergence is pushing capital toward MU and SNDK as cheaper, safer memory alternatives amid sector rotation.

bullets.title: Meta pricing 'Hatch' AI agent at up to $200/month; Muse Spark API repeatedly delayed
bullets.body: Meta is developing an AI agent product called 'Hatch' with premium pricing of up to $200/month, signaling a new high-margin revenue stream. However, Meta has delayed its Muse Spark AI API release multiple times with no fixed date, raising execution risk concerns.

bullets.title: MSFT: MAI signals vertical AI stack integration; false 200-day MA breakout flagged
bullets.body: Microsoft's MAI announcement is framed as a strategic move to control more of the AI production stack—including data infrastructure—not just a discrete model launch. Technically, MSFT traded above its 200-day moving average for one day then reversed lower, characterized as a failed breakout.

bullets.title: TSMC High-NA EUV: purchased but used for R&D only; economics not yet viable for production
bullets.body: TSMC CEO confirmed High-NA EUV equipment purchase but said current volumes do not justify production use—equipment deployed for research only. Intel 18A confirmed to be using Applied Materials' Centura Sculpta EUV pattern-shaping tool per TechInsights. Intel and Foxconn also announced a strategic AI infrastructure co-development partnership.

bullets.title: BOJ mulling June rate hike; 20-year JGB yield rises to 3.575%
bullets.body: BOJ is said to be mulling a rate hike at the June meeting with another possible in 2026, per Bloomberg sources. The 20-year JGB yield rose 4 bps to 3.575% and the 10-year to 2.67%, with Japan equity futures sliding 1.2% in early trade. BOJ is also reportedly inclined to ease the pace of bond-buying reduction starting fiscal 2027.

bullets.title: CPO commercialization timeline pushed to H2 2028; LITE signals CW laser bottleneck
bullets.body: One analyst argues CPO commercialization is unlikely before H2 2028—AMS, MediaTek and others are developing but still in early stages. LITE earnings signaled CW lasers are currently bottlenecked as laser fabs are heavily allocated to EML production. Passive optical components may be the next CPO supply constraint.

bullets.title: AMZN: 30,000 layoffs while building AI data centers; $1.25B Indiana data center announced
bullets.body: Amazon engineers in Seattle are criticizing the company for building new AI data centers while laying off 30,000 employees, flagging capital allocation tensions. Separately, Amazon announced a new data center in Wheatfield, Indiana, committing $1.25B to offset local energy cost impact.

bullets.title: AI server builders (DELL, HPE, SMCI) have thin margins on hardware boxes despite AI wave
bullets.body: An analysis flags that DELL, HPE, Lenovo, and SMCI are all riding the same AI infrastructure wave but the server boxes themselves have 'barely sustainable margins'—profit structures vary significantly and full analysis is forthcoming.

bullets.title: Agentic AI traffic accelerating faster than predicted; token spending surging to hundreds-thousands/employee
bullets.body: Multiple accounts note agentic traffic growth is accelerating ahead of predicted timelines (one source moved timeline from end-2027 to early-2027). Enterprise AI token spending is now reaching hundreds to thousands per employee per month versus prior $10-50/month software license costs—described as the hot topic among IT decision makers.
